---
title: "Cancer Basemap and Cancer InFocus"
---

Cancer InFocus (CIFTools, University of Kentucky Markey Cancer Center) is
the de facto standard tool NCI-designated centers already use to describe
their catchments. It covers every designated center, with 35 licensed
adopters as of October 2024 and an active community around the CARDS group
and the Catchment Area Data Conference. Cancer Basemap is not trying to
replace it.

## How the two projects relate

Cancer InFocus gathers county-level data and produces standardized files and
a Shiny app for a center's catchment; that's a strength this project doesn't
try to duplicate. What Cancer Basemap adds is a different kind of access:
every release stays queryable, joins across sources happen in SQL rather
than by hand, and the data is reachable from R, Python, SQL, a browser, or
an assistant, not only through one application.

The intended relationship: Cancer InFocus (or ECCO, or any center's own
tool) reads *from* Cancer Basemap, the same way a downstream consumer reads from
any published dataset. A recipe that writes CIFTools-shaped files for a
chosen catchment would fit that relationship better than a separate
dashboard, and the CARDS group is the audience this needs to reach before that recipe ships
([SPEC.md § Recipes](https://github.com/seandavi/cancer-basemap/blob/main/SPEC.md#recipes)
lists it as recipe 4, and open questions call out approaching the CIF team
directly before milestone M2 closes).

## What Cancer Basemap cannot carry

Cancer InFocus's own county-level cancer *incidence* comes from the USCS
Incidence Analytic Dataset through special access, a bilateral or
Research-Data-Center arrangement between the requester and CDC/NCI, not a
public redistribution license. A public dataset structurally cannot republish
that: the [license gate](license-gate.qmd) rules out anything that isn't
redistributable by a third party, and special-access USCS incidence fails
that test regardless of how the data would otherwise be used. What Cancer
Basemap carries instead is State Cancer Profiles' own *published* county
incidence and mortality rates. That is the same public route SCP itself
uses, and Cancer Basemap keeps it at every vintage rather than only the latest.

The ACR (American College of Radiology) Lung Cancer Screening Registry
facility locator is very likely proprietary and is not being pursued as a
source (SPEC.md's own license-gate table).

No Cancer InFocus data values, coverage figures, or comparisons appear on
this site. Anything about what CIF itself contains belongs to CIF and its
own documentation, not here.
